column1: # TA-neutrality allowlist -- the Phase 0 baseline. See docs/TA_NEUTRAL_DB_LAYER.md.
# EVERY VIOLATION LIVE ON 2026-08-30 IS LISTED HERE, so validate_ta_neutrality.py reports
# NEW = 0 on the day it ships. That is the whole design: the NEW count is the signal, and
# the KNOWN count is a debt ledger that can only go DOWN. You pay debt by DELETING a row --
# never by adding one to silence a finding you just created.
# The checker reports a row that no longer matches anything as STALE. Delete stale rows;
# they are how a baseline rots into a list of things that used to be true.
#   debt                the object is wrong and is scheduled. note names the phase.
#   archive             dead snapshot/backup table. Listed BY NAME -- a wildcard on
#                       %_backup would hide the next real violation that happens to be
#   per_ta_content      the NAME is a data-domain name; the TA-specific thing is the
#                       CONTENT, and it moves into per-TA rows in Phase 3 (design E).
#   false_positive      the scanner is wrong. No expiry.
#   ta_agnostic         genuinely TA-neutral already; the rule mis-fires on it.
#   slug_parameterised  parameterised, but by slug rather than uuid. Phase 4.
# expires: ISO date or '-'. A shim row past its expiry is reported as a violation again --
# that is what stops "temporary wrapper" from becoming permanent. Nothing here is a shim
# yet; the Phase 1 wrappers get dated rows when they are created.
# rule: 1..4, or * to exempt an object from all four.
